title: Hysteria 2: A QUIC Proxy Built for Bad Networks
metaTitle: What Is Hysteria 2? The QUIC Proxy Protocol Explained
metaDescription: Hysteria 2 explained: a proxy on QUIC that behaves like a real HTTP/3 web server to probes, holds speed on lossy networks, and fails where UDP or QUIC is blocked.
excerpt: A proxy on QUIC, the transport behind HTTP/3. Fast on lossy links, and a real HTTP/3 web server to anyone without the password. It needs UDP to get through.

apps.name: sing-box
apps.platforms: Cross-platform core used by several apps

faq.question: Is Hysteria 2 a VPN?
faq.answer: It is a proxy protocol, but clients such as Hiddify and NekoBox can route all of a device's traffic through it, so in practice it can be used like a VPN.

faq.question: Why is Hysteria 2 fast on bad connections?
faq.answer: It runs on QUIC over UDP, which recovers from packet loss without stalling every stream, and it can use its own congestion control aimed at unstable links.

faq.question: Can Hysteria 2 be blocked?
faq.answer: Probes see a real HTTP/3 server, so it resists active probing. But a censor can throttle or block UDP or QUIC broadly, and then Hysteria 2 cannot connect.

faq.question: Hysteria 2 or VLESS-Reality?
faq.answer: Hysteria 2 is often faster on lossy networks that allow UDP. VLESS-Reality runs over TCP and keeps working where UDP is filtered. Many people keep both.
